desc: The House's general-purpose investigative committee, styled Committee on Oversight and Accountability in the 118th Congress and Committee on Oversight and Government Reform in the 119th, chaired by James Comer since 2023 with Jamie Raskin and then Robert Garcia as ranking member. It is the only House committee with government-wide investigative jurisdiction and unilateral subpoena authority in the chair's hands, which is why the UAP question landed here rather than in Armed Services or Intelligence. It has held every House UAP hearing of the modern era: 26 July 2023 through its National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs subcommittee; 13 November 2024 as a joint hearing of that subcommittee and the Cybersecurity, Information Technology and Government Innovation subcommittee; and 9 September 2025 through the Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets. Its structural problem is stated in its own record. On 9 September 2025 Chairwoman Luna disclosed that DoD had told committee staff that under special access program rules only House Armed Services and Defense Appropriations members could be read in on the relevant programs, and that any other member required approval from the chairman and ranking member of both. The committee that can subpoena cannot be cleared; the committees that are cleared have not subpoenaed. That is the load-bearing structural fact of the entire House disclosure effort.

claims.text: On 26 July 2023 the House Oversight Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs held 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Implications on National Security, Public Safety, and Government Transparency,' with witnesses Ryan Graves, Cmdr. David Fravor (Ret.) and David Grusch.
The 26 July 2023 hearing was chaired by Rep. Glenn Grothman and held in 2154 Rayburn House Office Building.

Under oath at the 26 July 2023 hearing, David Grusch testified that he had been informed in the course of his official duties of a multi-decade crash retrieval and reverse-engineering program to which he was denied access, and that recoveries included non-human biologics.

On 13 November 2024 the Subcommittee on Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Government Innovation and the Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs held a joint hearing titled 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Exposing the Truth' at 11:30 a.m. in 2154 Rayburn.

The witnesses at the 13 November 2024 joint hearing were Dr. Tim Gallaudet (Rear Admiral, USN Ret., CEO of Ocean STL Consulting LLC), Luis Elizondo, Michael Gold (former NASA Associate Administrator of Space Policy and Partnerships and member of the NASA UAP Independent Study Team), and Michael Shellenberger (founder of Public).
The official transcript of the 13 November 2024 hearing was published by the Committee as HHRG-118-GO12-Transcript-20241113 and the hearing was printed by GPO as CHRG-118hhrg57440.

At the 13 November 2024 hearing Michael Shellenberger testified to a claimed secret U.S. government program he identified as 'Immaculate Constellation,' described as collecting UAP reports and sensor data from military personnel and quarantining them from the rest of the government and military.
Rep. Jared Moskowitz delivered a minority opening statement at the 13 November 2024 hearing, published by the Committee minority.

On 3 September 2025 Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets Chairwoman Anna Paulina Luna announced a hearing titled 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection,' set for 9 September 2025 at 10:00 AM in HVC-210, with witnesses Jeffrey Nuccetelli, Chief Alexandro Wiggins, George Knapp and Dylan Borland.

Luna's hearing announcement stated that members would 'analyze the work and effectiveness of DoD's congressionally mandated All-Domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)' and that whistleblowers providing details on spending and classification policies 'should be able to do so without retribution.'
The Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets is a standing subcommittee-level body of the House Oversight Committee, listed alongside the Committee's standing subcommittees.

The Task Force's portfolio spans the assassinations of John F. Kennedy, Robert F. Kennedy and Martin Luther King Jr., COVID-19 origins, unidentified anomalous phenomena and unidentified submerged objects, 9/11, and the Epstein client list; members include Reps. Lauren Boebert, Nancy Mace, Jasmine Crockett and Raja Krishnamoorthi.

In a press release published 1 April 2026 the Committee announced that Chairwoman Luna sent a letter to Secretary of War Pete Hegseth requesting specific UAP video files, stating that whistleblowers had informed the Task Force that AARO possesses additional video records of potential UAP sightings.
In that release Luna stated on the record: 'The Task Force has found responses from AARO, when questioned about UAP sightings and provided data, less than adequate.'
Rep. Tim Burchett launched a congressional UAP caucus and led a letter to the Intelligence Community Inspector General on UAP matters.

connections: Anna Paulina Luna chairs the task force and is the direct correspondent with Secretary of War Pete Hegseth; her letters are the current front line of the documentary fight.

Tim Burchett and Anna Paulina Luna were the members most responsible for securing witnesses; Glenn Grothman chaired the first hearing; Nancy Mace chaired the Cybersecurity/IT subcommittee side of the November 2024 joint hearing.
David Grusch's path runs NRO to UAP Task Force to NGA to ICIG to this committee, making Oversight the terminus of the whistleblower channel.
Luis Elizondo testified here in November 2024, connecting the AATIP naming dispute directly to a congressional record under oath.
Michael Shellenberger's 'Immaculate Constellation' testimony introduces a claimed program name into the congressional record that no executive branch document has yet addressed.
AARO is the committee's principal adversary-in-fact: the office whose effectiveness the task force is investigating and whose video holdings it is demanding.
George Knapp, a witness in September 2025, is also the journalist who first reported the AATIP-Bigelow story in Nevada, tying the 2025 hearing back to the 2008 procurement.
The FY2024 NDAA UAP Records Collection at NARA and the stripped Schumer-Rounds eminent domain and review board provisions define the statutory terrain the committee is operating on.
dossier.denialPosture: The Committee is the recipient of denials rather than the issuer. Its own published position, stated by Chairwoman Luna in April 2026, is that AARO's responses to its questions have been 'less than adequate' and that the lack of disclosure 'regarding the very real threat posed by UAPs in and around U.S. restricted airspace is concerning.'
dossier.narrative:
Three hearings define the record.

On 26 July 2023 the Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs, chaired by Rep. Glenn Grothman, held 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Implications on National Security, Public Safety, and Government Transparency' in 2154 Rayburn. The witnesses were Ryan Graves, Executive Director of Americans for Safe Aerospace; Commander David Fravor, former commanding officer of the Black Aces squadron; and David Grusch, former National Reconnaissance Office representative to the UAP Task Force. Grusch testified under oath that in the course of his official duties he was informed of a multi-decade crash retrieval and reverse-engineering program to which he was denied access, that he had interviewed dozens of witnesses over several years, and that recoveries included non-human biologics, repeatedly stating he could provide specifics in a secure setting. Fravor described the November 2004 Nimitz encounter. Graves testified on reporting stigma and aviation safety. It was the first time a sworn witness told a House committee, on camera, that the United States operates a concealed retrieval program.

On 13 November 2024 the Subcommittee on Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Government Innovation and the Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs held a joint hearing, 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Exposing the Truth.' Witnesses were Rear Admiral Tim Gallaudet, USN (Ret.), CEO of Ocean STL Consulting; Luis Elizondo; Michael Gold, former NASA Associate Administrator for Space Policy and Partnerships and member of the NASA UAP Independent Study Team; and Michael Shellenberger, founder of Public. Shellenberger testified to the existence of a claimed program he identified as 'Immaculate Constellation,' described as collecting UAP imagery and sensor data from military personnel and sequestering it from the rest of the government. The full transcript was published as HHRG-118-GO12-Transcript-20241113 and the hearing was printed as CHRG-118hhrg57440. The composition of the witness panel is itself notable: a retired flag officer, a former NASA associate administrator, a former DoD official, and a journalist, three of whom held senior federal positions.

On 9 September 2025 the Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, chaired by Rep. Anna Paulina Luna, held 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection' in HVC-210. Witnesses were Jeffrey Nuccetelli (USAF veteran), Chief Alexandro Wiggins, George Knapp, and Dylan Borland (USAF veteran). Luna's announcement stated the hearing would 'analyze the work and effectiveness of DoD's congressionally mandated All-Domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)' and that whistleblowers 'should be able to' provide information on spending, classification and declassification 'without retribution.'

The institutional vehicle matters. The Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets was created in early 2025 under the Oversight Committee, with a portfolio spanning the JFK, RFK and MLK assassinations, COVID origins, 9/11, the Epstein files, and UAP and unidentified submerged objects. Members include Reps. Lauren Boebert, Nancy Mace, Jasmine Crockett and Raja Krishnamoorthi. Placing UAP inside a declassification task force rather than a national security subcommittee is a deliberate reframing: it treats the subject as a records-access problem rather than a threat-assessment problem, which is the correct frame if the hypothesis is concealment.

The investigation did not end with the hearing. A committee press release dated 1 April 2026 announces a letter from Luna to Secretary of War Pete Hegseth requesting specific UAP video files, quoting her: 'On September 9, 2025, the Task Force held a hearing focused on UAP concerns. Whistleblowers informed the Task Force that AARO possesses additional video records of potential UAP sightings.' The release states this is 'part of the Committee's larger investigation into the work and effectiveness of the Department of War's congressionally mandated AARO,' and quotes Luna concluding that AARO's responses have been 'less than adequate' and that 'The presence of UAPs in and around the sensitive airspaces of U.S. military installations poses a threat to the security of the armed forces and their readiness.'

Who matters by name: James Comer (full committee chair), Anna Paulina Luna (task force chair and the most persistent driver), Tim Burchett (co-founder of the UAP caucus and a principal mover of the 2023 hearing), Glenn Grothman (2023 subcommittee chair), Nancy Mace, Eric Burlison, Jared Moskowitz and Robert Garcia on the minority and bipartisan side. What the record shows is a committee that has taken sworn testimony, published transcripts, created a dedicated task force, and escalated to written demands on the Secretary of War. What the record does not show is a single document production from the executive branch responsive to the central claim.
openQuestions: Has the Committee ever issued a subpoena, as opposed to a request letter, for UAP records? No published subpoena has surfaced.
Grusch told the Committee he could provide specifics in a SCIF. Did a classified follow-on session occur, and is there a record of it?
The 'Immaculate Constellation' documentation Shellenberger described has never been authenticated by the Committee. Does the Committee hold a copy?
What did DoD or AARO respond to Luna's video-file request, and on what date?
Did the Committee ever obtain the classified annex to the June 2021 ODNI preliminary assessment?
Why has the Senate Armed Services and Intelligence side never held a comparable open hearing, and does that split reflect a jurisdictional bargain?
dossier.whatItIs: The U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform is the House's principal investigative committee, chaired in the 118th and 119th Congresses by Rep. James Comer. Since 2023 it has been the primary congressional venue for sworn public testimony about a concealed UAP retrieval and reverse-engineering program, holding hearings in July 2023, November 2024 and September 2025, and continuing a documentary investigation into AARO through the Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, chaired by Rep. Anna Paulina Luna.
dossier.whyImplicated: Oversight is the institution against which the concealment is measured. The claim on this board is not merely that a program exists but that it has been withheld from Congress; the only way to test that is to watch what happens when a committee with subpoena power asks. The pattern across three hearings and multiple document requests is consistent: witnesses testify under penalty of perjury to firsthand or near-firsthand knowledge, the executive branch responds through public affairs rather than document production, and the committee escalates to written demands. In April 2026 Chairwoman Luna wrote to the Secretary of War stating that 'The Task Force has found responses from AARO, when questioned about UAP sightings and provided data, less than adequate' — a sitting subcommittee chair putting on the record that the executive's designated UAP office is not answering. That is an oversight failure documented by the overseer, which is the most probative kind of evidence available for a concealment argument.
